Delegation Mechanics: Legacy Dual-Sigmoid vs. Gaussian/Mobius Decision Model

A Technical Reference for the Liquid Democracy Simulation (accompanies Report 20)

2026-07-30

1 Purpose and Scope

This note is a self-contained technical reference explaining the delegation-decision mechanics of the liquid-democracy simulation, comparing the legacy dual-sigmoid model (used in Reports 15-19) against the new Gaussian-opinion / Mobius-self-vote model introduced for Report 20 (decision_model = "gaussian_mobius" in simulate_liquid_democracy()).

Both formula sets are switched with a single argument; everything else in the simulation – network construction, the trust update, ingroup preference, cycle handling, homophily shuffling, and all recorded metrics – is completely unchanged between the two models. This note therefore focuses exclusively on the one part of the model that did change: how attractive a neighbour looks to an agent, and how that agent decides whether to vote directly or delegate.

Throughout, \(i\) is the focal agent, \(j\) ranges over \(i\)’s network neighbours, \(o\) denotes opinion, \(p\) denotes current voting power, and \(j^\*= \arg\max_j A_{ij}\) is \(i\)’s single most attractive neighbour.

2 Part I – The New Decision Model (gaussian_mobius)

2.1 Overview: the three-step pipeline

Every round, for every lay agent \(i\) with at least one neighbour, the simulation resolves a delegation decision in three steps:

Step 1 computes a full vector of attractivenesses (one per neighbour). Step 2 collapses that vector to a single scalar \(m\) (the best neighbour’s attractiveness) and maps it to a self-vote probability. Step 3 draws a Bernoulli(\(P_{\text{self}}\)) coin; on failure, agent \(i\) delegates to a neighbour sampled proportional to attractiveness. This is a genuine information bottleneck: Step 2 never looks at who \(j^\*\) is (their opinion, their power) – only at how attractive they are. Keep this in mind; it is the single biggest structural difference from the legacy model, discussed at length in Part III.

2.2 Step 1: Attractiveness

\[A_{ij} = 2\,\tau_{ij}\,a^{\text{op}}_{ij}\,a^{\text{pw}}_{ij}\]

implemented as attractiveness_gaussian_log() in FunctionVersions.R. It returns \(2\,a^{\text{op}}_{ij}\,a^{\text{pw}}_{ij}\); the trust factor \(\tau_{ij}\) is applied afterwards, exactly as for every other attractiveness formula in this codebase (see Part I.5).

2.2.1 Opinion factor: a Gaussian kernel

\[a^{\text{op}}_{ij} = \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\,r_{op}^2\,(o_i - o_j)^2\right)\]

This is a Gaussian bump centred on \(o_i\) with standard deviation \(\sigma_{\text{op}} = 1/r_{op}\): it equals exactly \(1\) when \(j\)’s opinion is identical to \(i\)’s, and decays smoothly to \(0\) as the opinion gap grows. \(r_{op}\) is an inverse width: larger \(r_{op}\) means a narrower, more selective bump (only near-identical neighbours count as attractive); smaller \(r_{op}\) means a wide, forgiving bump (almost any neighbour scores close to 1 on the opinion dimension).

op_dist <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 300)
r_op_vals <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)

df_op_new <- expand_grid(delta = op_dist, r_op = r_op_vals) |>
  # attractiveness_gaussian_log(op_i, op_j, pow_i, pow_j, r_op, r_pw): with
  # pow_i = pow_j = 1, a_pw = sig(0) = 0.5 exactly, so dividing the real
  # production function's output by 0.5 recovers a_op(delta) in isolation --
  # this is the ACTUAL sourced function, not a re-derivation.
  mutate(a_op = attractiveness_gaussian_log(0, delta, 1, 1, r_op, 1) / 0.5,
         r_op_label = factor(paste0("r_op = ", r_op), levels = paste0("r_op = ", r_op_vals)))

ggplot(df_op_new, aes(delta, a_op, colour = r_op_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(title = "New opinion factor a_op(Delta) -- Gaussian kernel",
       subtitle = "a_op = exp(-0.5 * r_op^2 * Delta^2); Delta = |o_i - o_j|",
       x = expression(Delta == "|"*o[i]-o[j]*"|"), y = expression(a[op]),
       colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Numeric example. At \(r_{op}=4\):

tibble(Delta = c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)) |>
  mutate(a_op = attractiveness_gaussian_log(0, Delta, 1, 1, 4, 1) / 0.5) |>
  kable(digits = 4, col.names = c("Opinion distance $\\Delta$", "$a^{\\text{op}}$ (r_op = 4)"))
Opinion distance \(\Delta\) \(a^{\text{op}}\) (r_op = 4)
0.00 2.0000
0.10 1.8462
0.25 1.2131
0.50 0.2707
0.75 0.0222
1.00 0.0007

A neighbour half a unit away on the \([0,1]\) opinion scale is already down to about 3% attractiveness at this responsiveness level – opinion gating is aggressive once \(r_{op}\) is moderately large.

2.2.2 Power factor: unchanged from the legacy model

\[a^{\text{pw}}_{ij} = \sigma\!\left(r_{pw}\,\log\frac{p_j}{p_i}\right), \qquad \sigma(x) = \frac{1}{1+e^{-x}}\]

This half of the formula is identical in form to the legacy model (Part II) – a sigmoid of the log power ratio. It equals \(0.5\) when \(i\) and \(j\) hold equal power, saturates toward \(1\) as \(j\) becomes arbitrarily more powerful, and toward \(0\) as \(j\) becomes negligible. \(r_{pw}\) is the steepness of that saturation.

pow_ratio <- 10^seq(-2, 2, length.out = 300)
r_pw_vals <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4)

df_pw <- expand_grid(ratio = pow_ratio, r_pw = r_pw_vals) |>
  # Delta_op = 0 forces a_op = 1 exactly, so the real function's output /
  # 2 isolates a_pw(ratio). This is the SAME function used for the legacy
  # power factor -- see Part II.2.
  mutate(a_pw = attractiveness_gaussian_log(0, 0, 1, ratio, 1, r_pw) / 2,
         r_pw_label = factor(paste0("r_pw = ", r_pw), levels = paste0("r_pw = ", r_pw_vals)))

ggplot(df_pw, aes(ratio, a_pw, colour = r_pw_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85, option = "magma") +
  labs(title = "Power factor a_pw(power ratio) -- identical in old and new models",
       subtitle = "a_pw = sig(r_pw * log(p_j / p_i)); = 0.5 at equal power (dotted lines)",
       x = expression(p[j]/p[i]~"(log scale)"), y = expression(a[pw]), colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

tibble(ratio = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10)) |>
  mutate(a_pw = attractiveness_gaussian_log(0, 0, 1, ratio, 1, 2) / 2) |>
  kable(digits = 4, col.names = c("Power ratio $p_j/p_i$", "$a^{\\text{pw}}$ (r_pw = 2)"))
Power ratio \(p_j/p_i\) \(a^{\text{pw}}\) (r_pw = 2)
0.1 0.0099
0.5 0.2000
1.0 0.5000
2.0 0.8000
10.0 0.9901

2.3 Step 2: Self-vote probability – the Mobius curve

Let \(m_i = \max_j A_{ij}\) (the attractiveness of \(i\)’s single best neighbour, on the \([0,2]\) scale established above). The self-vote probability is:

\[P_{\text{self}}(m) = \frac{2 - m}{\,2 + \dfrac{1-2c}{c}\,m\,}\]

implemented as p_self_mobius(). It is a Mobius (rational-linear) transform pinned at three anchors:

best neighbour \(m\) \(P_{\text{self}}\) meaning
nightmare \(0\) \(1\) always self-vote
identical to me \(1\) \(c\) self-reliance knob
perfect \(2\) \(0\) always delegate

\(c \in (0,1)\) is the entire free parameter of this step: it is set directly (self_reliance_c in simulate_liquid_democracy()) and does not depend on \(r_{op}\), \(r_{pw}\), or anything about \(j^\*\) specifically – see Part III.2 for why this matters.

m_grid <- seq(0, 2, length.out = 300)
c_vals <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8)

df_pself <- expand_grid(m = m_grid, c = c_vals) |>
  mutate(P_self = p_self_mobius(m, c),
         c_label = factor(paste0("c = ", c), levels = paste0("c = ", c_vals)))

ggplot(df_pself, aes(m, P_self, colour = c_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = tibble(m = c(0, 1, 2), P_self = c(1, NA, 0)),
             aes(m, P_self), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey30", size = 0, alpha = 0) +
  annotate("point", x = 0, y = 1, colour = "grey20", size = 2) +
  annotate("point", x = 2, y = 0, colour = "grey20", size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.05, y = 1.04, label = "m=0 -> always self-vote", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.95, y = 0.06, label = "m=2 -> always delegate", hjust = 1, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85, option = "plasma") +
  labs(title = "Self-vote probability P_self(m) -- Mobius curve",
       subtitle = "m = attractiveness of the single best neighbour, on [0,2]",
       x = expression(m == max[j]~A[ij]), y = expression(P[self]), colour = "self-reliance c") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Numeric example. At \(m=1\) (an exactly identical best neighbour), \(P_{\text{self}} = c\) by construction, for every value of \(r_{op}\) and \(r_{pw}\):

tibble(c = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8)) |>
  mutate(`P_self(m=1)` = p_self_mobius(1, c)) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
c P_self(m=1)
0.1 0.1
0.2 0.2
0.5 0.5
0.8 0.8

2.4 Step 3: Delegate choice

Conditional on not self-voting, \(i\) delegates to a neighbour sampled with probability proportional to \(A_{ij}\) among its real (non-padding) neighbours – a straightforward weighted draw, structurally identical to the legacy model’s delegate-choice step (nb[sample.int(length(w), 1L, prob = w)] in Network.R, unchanged by decision_model). What differs between the two models is only the shape of the weights being sampled from, not the sampling rule itself.

A_vals <- c(j1 = 0.2, j2 = 0.8, j3 = 1.5, j4 = 0.1)
df_choice <- tibble(neighbour = names(A_vals), A = A_vals) |>
  mutate(P_delegate_to = A / sum(A))

ggplot(df_choice, aes(neighbour, P_delegate_to, fill = neighbour)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("A=%.1f\nP=%.2f", A, P_delegate_to)), vjust = -0.15, size = 3.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, max(df_choice$P_delegate_to) * 1.35)) +
  labs(title = "Delegate choice: weighted sampling proportional to A_ij (illustrative example)",
       subtitle = "4 neighbours with attractivenesses 0.2, 0.8, 1.5, 0.1 -> delegation probabilities, given not self-voting",
       x = NULL, y = "P(delegate to j | delegating)")

2.5 Trust interaction (unchanged mechanism, recap only)

Trust is not part of the new formula set – it is the existing Report 18 mechanism, applied identically regardless of decision_model:

\[\texttt{trust\_mod}_{ij} = 2\,\sigma(\gamma\,\tau_{ij}), \qquad w_{ij} = \texttt{trust\_mod}_{ij} \times A_{ij}\]

with \(\tau_{ij}\) updated each round via the punish_only / reward_punish rules documented in Network.R. trust_mod = 1 (neutral) when \(\gamma=0\) or \(\tau_{ij}=0\); it can exceed \(1\) (boosting a well-trusted neighbour) or fall toward \(0\) (suppressing a mistrusted one).

tau_grid <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 200)
gamma_vals <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4)

df_trust <- expand_grid(tau = tau_grid, gamma = gamma_vals) |>
  mutate(trust_mod = 2 * .sig(gamma * tau),
         gamma_label = factor(paste0("gamma = ", gamma), levels = paste0("gamma = ", gamma_vals)))

ggplot(df_trust, aes(tau, trust_mod, colour = gamma_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick3") +
  annotate("text", x = -2.8, y = 2.05, label = "trust_mod ceiling = 2", colour = "firebrick3", size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85, option = "cividis") +
  labs(title = "trust_mod(tau) = 2*sig(gamma*tau) -- unchanged in both decision models",
       x = expression(tau[ij]), y = "trust_mod", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Note the dashed ceiling at \(\texttt{trust\_mod}=2\): this will matter in Part III.6, because the new model’s \(m\) is computed from the trust-adjusted weight \(w_{j^\*}\), not the raw attractiveness.

2.6 Parameter glossary (new model)

tibble(
  Parameter = c("r_op", "r_pw", "self_reliance_c", "gamma", "lambda", "trust_mode"),
  Controls = c(
    "Inverse width of the Gaussian opinion kernel a_op. Larger = narrower = more opinion-selective.",
    "Steepness of the power-ratio sigmoid a_pw. Larger = more power-deferential.",
    "Self-reliance knob c in the Mobius P_self curve. Larger = more self-reliant (delegates only to clearly-better neighbours). Independent of r_op/r_pw.",
    "Trust sensitivity: how strongly accumulated trust tau rescales attractiveness (unchanged mechanism).",
    "Trust decay/momentum: how much of last round's tau carries over (unchanged mechanism).",
    "'punish_only' or 'reward_punish' trust update rule (unchanged mechanism)."
  ),
  `Typical range` = c("0.5 - 8", "0.5 - 8", "0.1 - 0.9 (open interval)", "0 (off) - 8", "0 - 1", "categorical")
) |>
  kable()

3 Part II – Recap: The Legacy Dual-Sigmoid Model

Reports 15-19 use decision_model = "legacy" (the default), summarised here for direct comparison.

3.1 Attractiveness (dual sigmoid)

\[A_{ij} = \sigma\big(r_{op}(1-2|o_i-o_j|)\big)\,\times\,\sigma\!\left(r_{pw}\log\frac{p_j}{p_i}\right)\]

implemented as attractiveness_dual_sigmoid(). Both factors are sigmoids: opinion similarity \(1-2|o_i-o_j|\) is remapped from \([-1,1]\) (identical to maximally distant) through a sigmoid, and the power factor is the same log-ratio sigmoid used in the new model.

df_op_old <- expand_grid(delta = op_dist, r_op = r_op_vals) |>
  mutate(a_op = attractiveness_dual_sigmoid(0, delta, 1, 1, r_op, 1) / 0.5,
         r_op_label = factor(paste0("r_op = ", r_op), levels = paste0("r_op = ", r_op_vals)))

ggplot(df_op_old, aes(delta, a_op, colour = r_op_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.51, y = 0.95, label = "fixed midpoint\nDelta = 0.5", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(title = "Legacy opinion factor a_op(Delta) -- sigmoid of similarity",
       subtitle = "a_op = sig(r_op * (1 - 2*Delta)); always crosses exactly 0.5 at Delta = 0.5",
       x = expression(Delta == "|"*o[i]-o[j]*"|"), y = expression(a[op]), colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

The power factor \(a^{\text{pw}}\) is the identical function already plotted in Part I.2 – the legacy and new models do not differ on the power dimension at all.

3.2 Self-weight (dual-sigmoid argmax) and the “confidence” patch

Given \(j^\*=\arg\max_j A_{ij}\) (found using the same attractiveness weights as Step 3), the legacy self-weight is a second, independent formula that re-derives a weight from \(j^\*\)’s specific opinion and power gap – it does not reuse \(A_{ij^\*}\) directly:

\[w^{\text{raw}}_{\text{self}} = \sigma\big(r_{op}(2|o_i-o_{j^\*}|-1)\big) \times \sigma\!\left(r_{pw}\log\frac{p_i}{p_{j^\*}}\right)\]

This is a mirror image of the attractiveness formula (opinion sign flipped: far away \(\Rightarrow\) high self-confidence). self_weight_mode controls what happens next:

  • "raw": use \(w^{\text{raw}}_{\text{self}}\) as-is.
  • "confidence" (used in Reports 17-19): blend it toward “always self-vote” using a saturating function of total responsiveness \(r_{\text{tot}} = r_{op}+r_{pw}+r_{ingroup}\) (or their mean, per confidence_agg):

\[\text{conf} = \frac{r_{\text{tot}}}{1+r_{\text{tot}}}, \qquad w_{\text{self}} = (1-\text{conf}) + \text{conf}\cdot w^{\text{raw}}_{\text{self}}\]

This blending step exists to fix a specific, documented artefact: at \(r_{op}=r_{pw}=0\) (no responsiveness at all), \(w^{\text{raw}}_{\text{self}} = \sigma(0)\cdot\sigma(0) = 0.25\) exactly – a floor that keeps roughly a quarter of agents self-voting even when nobody cares about opinion or power at all, which is not a meaningful behavioural claim, just an artefact of multiplying two sigmoids evaluated at zero. "confidence" mode papers over this by interpolating toward \(1\) (self-vote) as responsiveness \(\to 0\).

tibble(r = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)) |>
  mutate(
    `w_self_raw (identical j*)` = .sig(r * (2 * 0 - 1)) * .sig(r * log(1)),
    `confidence blend (r_ingroup=0)` = {
      conf <- (2 * r) / (1 + 2 * r)  # r_tot = r_op + r_pw = 2r here
      (1 - conf) + conf * `w_self_raw (identical j*)`
    }
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 4)
r w_self_raw (identical j*) confidence blend (r_ingroup=0)
0.0 0.2500 1.0000
0.5 0.1888 0.5944
1.0 0.1345 0.4230
2.0 0.0596 0.2477
4.0 0.0090 0.1191
8.0 0.0002 0.0590 
r_seq <- seq(0, 8, length.out = 200)
df_conf <- tibble(r = r_seq) |>
  mutate(
    w_raw = .sig(r * (2 * 0 - 1)) * .sig(r * log(1)),
    conf  = (2 * r) / (1 + 2 * r),
    w_confidence = (1 - conf) + conf * w_raw
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(w_raw, w_confidence), names_to = "mode", values_to = "w_self") |>
  mutate(mode = recode(mode, w_raw = "raw", w_confidence = "confidence"))

ggplot(df_conf, aes(r, w_self, colour = mode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.25, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.1, y = 0.27, label = "0.25 floor (raw mode)", size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(raw = "#d95f02", confidence = "#1b9e77")) +
  labs(title = "Legacy self-weight at an identical best neighbour, vs. responsiveness r = r_op = r_pw",
       subtitle = "'raw' mode floors at 0.25 as r -> 0; 'confidence' mode fixes this by interpolating toward self-vote",
       x = "r (= r_op = r_pw)", y = expression(w[self]), colour = "self_weight_mode") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

3.3 Delegate choice

Identical mechanism to Part I.4 – weighted sampling proportional to \(A_{ij}\), unaffected by decision_model.

3.4 Parameter glossary (legacy model)

tibble(
  Parameter = c("r_op", "r_pw", "self_weight_mode", "confidence_agg", "r_ingroup", "gamma / lambda / trust_mode"),
  Controls = c(
    "Steepness of the opinion-similarity sigmoid AND (via the mirrored formula) part of self-confidence.",
    "Steepness of the power-ratio sigmoid AND (via the mirrored formula) part of self-confidence.",
    "'raw' (use w_self_raw as-is) or 'confidence' (blend toward always-self-vote at low responsiveness).",
    "'sum' or 'mean' -- how r_op/r_pw/r_ingroup combine into r_tot for the confidence blend.",
    "Ingroup responsiveness -- multiplies attractiveness by sig(+-r_ingroup), also feeds r_tot.",
    "Same trust mechanism as the new model, unaffected by decision_model."
  )
) |>
  kable()
Parameter Controls
r_op Steepness of the opinion-similarity sigmoid AND (via the mirrored formula) part of self-confidence.
r_pw Steepness of the power-ratio sigmoid AND (via the mirrored formula) part of self-confidence.
self_weight_mode ‘raw’ (use w_self_raw as-is) or ‘confidence’ (blend toward always-self-vote at low responsiveness).

4 Part III – Detailed Comparison

4.1 III.1 What changed, in one table

tibble(
  Component = c("Opinion factor", "Power factor", "Self-vote step",
                "Self-vote inputs", "Delegate choice", "Trust interaction"),
  Legacy = c(
    "$\\sigma(r_{op}(1-2\\Delta))$ -- sigmoid, fixed midpoint at $\\Delta=0.5$",
    "$\\sigma(r_{pw}\\log(p_j/p_i))$",
    "Re-derived formula, mirror of attractiveness, evaluated at $j^*$'s raw $(o_{j^*}, p_{j^*})$",
    "2 numbers: $\\Delta(i,j^*)$ and power ratio $(i,j^*)$, both fed through $r_{op}, r_{pw}$ again",
    "Sample $\\propto A_{ij}$ among neighbours",
    "trust_mod multiplies $A_{ij}$ (affects $j^*$ selection and sampling only)"
  ),
  `Gaussian/Mobius` = c(
    "$\\exp(-\\tfrac12 r_{op}^2\\Delta^2)$ -- Gaussian, $r_{op}$-dependent half-width",
    "$\\sigma(r_{pw}\\log(p_j/p_i))$ -- unchanged",
    "$P_{\\text{self}}(m)$, Mobius curve, single free parameter $c$",
    "1 number: $m = A_{ij^*}$ (already includes trust/ingroup)",
    "Sample $\\propto A_{ij}$ among neighbours -- unchanged",
    "trust_mod multiplies $A_{ij}$, feeding directly into $m$ (see III.6)"
  )
) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE)
Component Legacy Gaussian/Mobius
Opinion factor \(\sigma(r_{op}(1-2\Delta))\) – sigmoid, fixed midpoint at \(\Delta=0.5\) \(\exp(-\tfrac12 r_{op}^2\Delta^2)\) – Gaussian, \(r_{op}\)-dependent half-width
Power factor \(\sigma(r_{pw}\log(p_j/p_i))\) \(\sigma(r_{pw}\log(p_j/p_i))\) – unchanged
Self-vote step Re-derived formula, mirror of attractiveness, evaluated at \(j^*\)’s raw \((o_{j^*}, p_{j^*})\) \(P_{\text{self}}(m)\), Mobius curve, single free parameter \(c\)
Self-vote inputs 2 numbers: \(\Delta(i,j^*)\) and power ratio \((i,j^*)\), both fed through \(r_{op}, r_{pw}\) again 1 number: \(m = A_{ij^*}\) (already includes trust/ingroup)
Delegate choice Sample \(\propto A_{ij}\) among neighbours Sample \(\propto A_{ij}\) among neighbours – unchanged
Trust interaction trust_mod multiplies \(A_{ij}\) (affects \(j^*\) selection and sampling only) trust_mod multiplies \(A_{ij}\), feeding directly into \(m\) (see III.6)

The power factor and the delegate-choice mechanism are literally the same code in both models. Everything else changed. The next five subsections unpack why each change matters.

4.2 III.2 Ceiling non-equivalence: what does “identical neighbour” mean?

An identical neighbour (\(\Delta=0\), equal power) is the natural reference point for “as attractive as it gets, ideologically.” The two models treat it very differently:

r_seq2 <- seq(0.25, 16, length.out = 200)
df_ceiling <- tibble(r = r_seq2) |>
  mutate(
    old = attractiveness_dual_sigmoid(0, 0, 1, 1, r, r),
    new = attractiveness_gaussian_log(0, 0, 1, 1, r, r)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(old, new), names_to = "model", values_to = "A_identical")

ggplot(df_ceiling, aes(r, A_identical, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 1), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(old = "#d95f02", new = "#1b9e77"),
                       labels = c(old = "legacy (dual sigmoid)", new = "gaussian_mobius")) +
  labs(title = "Attractiveness of an IDENTICAL neighbour (Delta=0, equal power), vs. r = r_op = r_pw",
       subtitle = "New model: always exactly 1. Legacy model: rises toward 0.5 only as r -> infinity",
       x = "r (= r_op = r_pw)", y = expression(A[ij]~"(identical neighbour)"), colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

At \(r=4\) (a typical “responsive” setting used throughout Reports 17-19), an identical neighbour scores \(A \approx\) 0.491 under the legacy model but exactly \(1\) under the new one. The new model’s “1” is an invariant reference point, independent of \(r_{op}, r_{pw}\); the legacy model’s ceiling is itself a function of responsiveness, and never actually reaches even \(0.5\) at finite \(r\). This is a direct, mechanical consequence of multiplying two sigmoids that individually saturate below 1 rather than a Gaussian that reaches exactly 1 at zero distance.

4.3 III.3 Decoupling: is self-reliance its own parameter, or entangled with \(r\)?

This is the most consequential conceptual change. Evaluate each model’s self-vote quantity specifically at the “identical best neighbour” case (\(m=1\) for the new model; \(\Delta=0\), ratio\(=1\) for the legacy formula):

df_decouple_old <- tibble(r = r_seq2) |>
  mutate(w_self = .sig(r * (2 * 0 - 1)) * .sig(r * log(1)), model = "legacy")

df_decouple_new <- expand_grid(r = r_seq2, c = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)) |>
  mutate(w_self = p_self_mobius(1, c), model = paste0("gaussian_mobius, c=", c))

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = df_decouple_old, aes(r, w_self, colour = model), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(data = df_decouple_new, aes(r, w_self, colour = model), linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("legacy" = "#d95f02",
                                 "gaussian_mobius, c=0.2" = "#1b9e77",
                                 "gaussian_mobius, c=0.5" = "#377eb8",
                                 "gaussian_mobius, c=0.8" = "#984ea3")) +
  labs(title = "Self-vote probability at an IDENTICAL best neighbour, vs. background responsiveness r",
       subtitle = "Legacy: entangled with r, collapses toward 0 as r grows. New: flat -- exactly c, for any r",
       x = "r (= r_op = r_pw, legacy only)", y = expression(P[self]~"or"~w[self]~"(identical best neighbour)"),
       colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Under the legacy model, self-reliance when facing an identical neighbour is not a free choice – it is whatever falls out of \(r_{op}, r_{pw}\), which also simultaneously control how sharply opinion/power gate attractiveness. Turning up “how much do I care about opinion similarity” (raising \(r_{op}\)) automatically and inescapably turns down “how likely am I to still vote for myself when facing someone just like me” (from \(0.25\) at \(r=0\) down to essentially \(0\) by \(r\approx8\), confirmed numerically above). There is no way, in the legacy model, to have a highly opinion-selective agent who is also strongly self-reliant, short of the "confidence" patch, which addresses only the \(r\to0\) floor, not this coupling.

The new model removes this coupling entirely: \(c\) is set independently and \(P_{\text{self}}(m{=}1)=c\) for every \(r_{op}\). An agent can be extremely opinion-selective (\(r_{op}=8\)) and still self-reliant (\(c=0.8\)) simultaneously – a combination that is difficult to reach in the legacy model and impossible to reach exactly by construction.

4.4 III.4 Where does \(r_{op}\) actually act? A hidden non-equivalence

Both models expose an argument literally called r_op, swept over the same values in Report 20 as in Report 19 (\(1, 4, 8\)). These are not comparable in the same units. Consider the opinion distance at which \(a^{\text{op}}=0.5\) (the “half-attractiveness point”):

  • Legacy: \(\sigma(r_{op}(1-2\Delta))=0.5 \iff \Delta = 0.5\), for every value of \(r_{op}\). \(r_{op}\) only controls how sharply the curve transitions around that fixed midpoint – it never moves.
  • New: \(\exp(-\tfrac12 r_{op}^2\Delta^2)=0.5 \iff \Delta = \sqrt{2\ln2}/r_{op} \approx 1.1774/r_{op}\) – the half-attractiveness point moves inward as \(r_{op}\) grows.
r_seq3 <- seq(0.25, 16, length.out = 200)
df_half <- tibble(r = r_seq3) |>
  mutate(legacy = 0.5, new = sqrt(2 * log(2)) / r) |>
  pivot_longer(c(legacy, new), names_to = "model", values_to = "half_distance")

ggplot(df_half, aes(r, half_distance, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(legacy = "#d95f02", new = "#1b9e77")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Half-attractiveness distance (where a_op = 0.5), vs. r_op",
       subtitle = "Legacy: r_op controls STEEPNESS at a FIXED reference point (Delta=0.5).\nNew: r_op controls the LOCATION of the reference point (an inverse bandwidth).",
       x = "r_op", y = expression("opinion distance"~Delta~"where"~a[op]==0.5), colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Practical consequence: “\(r_{op}=8\)” means “a sharp step exactly at \(\Delta=0.5\)” in the legacy model, but “a narrow bump that has already collapsed by \(\Delta\approx0.15\)” in the new model. Report 20 sweeps the same numeric values as Report 19 for continuity, but any claim of the form “the effect of \(r_{op}\) is X in both models” should be read as label-comparable, not magnitude-comparable, unless the sweep is re-calibrated via the mapping above (see Part VII.3 for a concrete fix).

4.5 III.5 Sharper echo chambers?

Because the new model’s opinion gate is genuinely bounded away from the legacy sigmoid’s shallow tails (a Gaussian’s tail decays like \(e^{-\Delta^2}\), faster than a sigmoid’s like \(e^{-\Delta}\) for large arguments), a highly polarised, highly opinion-responsive population is expected to show attractiveness collapsing faster across an opinion gap under gaussian_mobius than under legacy, at matched nominal \(r_{op}\). Combined with III.4 (the new model’s bandwidth also shrinks with \(r_{op}\), compounding the effect), this predicts: more baseline opinion-driven self-segregation under the new model, before ingroup preference (\(r_{ingroup}\)) is even switched on. This is directly relevant to Report 20’s hypotheses – see Part V.

4.6 III.6 A genuine edge case: trust can push \(m\) past its designed ceiling

Recall from Part I.5 that \(\texttt{trust\_mod} = 2\sigma(\gamma\tau)\) can itself range up to (not including) \(2\). In the legacy model, trust only ever affects (a) which neighbour becomes \(j^\*\) (the argmax is computed over trust-adjusted weights) and (b) the delegate-choice sampling weights. The self-weight formula in Step 2 is recomputed from scratch from \(j^\*\)’s raw opinion/power gap – it never sees the trust-adjusted number itself, so it is mathematically guaranteed to stay in \([0,1]\) (a product of two sigmoids) regardless of how extreme trust becomes.

The new model’s Step 2 uses \(m = w_{j^\*}\) directly – the trust-adjusted attractiveness. If trust pushes a neighbour’s weight above the formula’s designed ceiling of \(2\) (entirely possible: \(A_{ij}\le2\) times \(\texttt{trust\_mod}<2\) can exceed \(2\)), the Mobius formula extrapolates outside its intended domain:

m_ext <- seq(0, 3, length.out = 300)
df_edge <- tibble(m = m_ext) |> mutate(P_self = p_self_mobius(m, 0.5))

ggplot(df_edge, aes(m, P_self)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 2, xmax = 3, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), fill = "#fdecea", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, colour = "#377eb8") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick3") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.05, y = 0.35, label = "beyond designed ceiling\n(trust-boosted m > 2)\nP_self < 0 -> treated\nas 'never self-vote'",
           hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "firebrick4") +
  labs(title = "p_self_mobius(m, c=0.5) extrapolated beyond the nominal [0,2] domain",
       x = expression(m == w[j^"*"]~"(trust-adjusted)"), y = expression(P[self]))

tibble(m = c(0, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3)) |>
  mutate(P_self = p_self_mobius(m, 0.5)) |>
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "P_self(m, c=0.5): note the sign flip past m=2")
P_self(m, c=0.5): note the sign flip past m=2
m P_self
0.0 1.00
1.0 0.50
1.5 0.25
2.0 0.00
2.5 -0.25
3.0 -0.50

Negative \(P_{\text{self}}\) is not a crash – runif(1) < P_self is simply always FALSE for a negative threshold, so the practical effect is “always delegate,” which is arguably the intended direction (a strongly-trust-boosted neighbour should be very delegate-worthy) but is reached through an out-of-domain formula evaluation rather than by design. This is flagged explicitly as a concrete, fixable weakness in Part VII.

5 Part IV – Advantages and Disadvantages

tibble(
  Criterion = c("Realism", "Interpretability", "Flexibility", "Robustness",
                "Computational complexity", "Ease of parameter tuning"),
  `Legacy (dual sigmoid)` = c(
    "Sigmoid saturation is a common choice-model primitive (logistic response); opinion cutoff shape is arguably less 'natural' than a bell curve of similarity.",
    "Single family of parameters (r_op, r_pw, r_ingroup) drives everything, but the self-weight formula's meaning is only clear once you see it's a 'mirror' of attractiveness -- non-obvious on first read.",
    "self_weight_mode/confidence_agg add two more categorical switches on top of r_op/r_pw to reach a full delegation-rate range -- flexible, but via a layered patch rather than a single mechanism.",
    "Self-weight is always a valid probability in [0,1] by construction, regardless of how extreme trust or attractiveness become -- no known domain violations.",
    "One extra sigmoid evaluation per agent per round vs. the new model -- negligible difference either way.",
    "r_op/r_pw jointly govern opinion gating AND self-reliance -- tuning one for a target delegation rate can silently distort the other."
  ),
  `Gaussian/Mobius` = c(
    "Gaussian opinion kernel matches a natural 'similarity as closeness in a metric space' intuition; Mobius curve is a clean, purpose-built interpolant with named anchors rather than an emergent by-product of two sigmoids.",
    "Anchors (m=0->1, m=1->c, m=2->0) are directly readable off the formula; c has a literal meaning ('self-vote probability when facing an identical neighbour') independent of anything else.",
    "c is a single, dedicated self-reliance knob -- can be swept independently of r_op/r_pw without any patch or blending logic.",
    "m can exceed the formula's designed [0,2] ceiling under strong reward+punish trust, producing negative (out-of-domain) probabilities -- see III.6. Rare, but real and currently unguarded.",
    "Same order of cost (one exp(), one division) -- negligible difference either way.",
    "c alone controls self-reliance; r_op/r_pw only shape the opinion/power kernels -- but r_op's meaning is not comparable across models (III.4), complicating any joint calibration against legacy results."
  )
) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE)
Criterion Legacy (dual sigmoid) Gaussian/Mobius
Realism Sigmoid saturation is a common choice-model primitive (logistic response); opinion cutoff shape is arguably less ‘natural’ than a bell curve of similarity. Gaussian opinion kernel matches a natural ‘similarity as closeness in a metric space’ intuition; Mobius curve is a clean, purpose-built interpolant with named anchors rather than an emergent by-product of two sigmoids.
Interpretability Single family of parameters (r_op, r_pw, r_ingroup) drives everything, but the self-weight formula’s meaning is only clear once you see it’s a ‘mirror’ of attractiveness – non-obvious on first read. Anchors (m=0->1, m=1->c, m=2->0) are directly readable off the formula; c has a literal meaning (‘self-vote probability when facing an identical neighbour’) independent of anything else.
Flexibility self_weight_mode/confidence_agg add two more categorical switches on top of r_op/r_pw to reach a full delegation-rate range – flexible, but via a layered patch rather than a single mechanism. c is a single, dedicated self-reliance knob – can be swept independently of r_op/r_pw without any patch or blending logic.
Robustness Self-weight is always a valid probability in [0,1] by construction, regardless of how extreme trust or attractiveness become – no known domain violations. m can exceed the formula’s designed [0,2] ceiling under strong reward+punish trust, producing negative (out-of-domain) probabilities – see III.6. Rare, but real and currently unguarded.
Computational complexity One extra sigmoid evaluation per agent per round vs. the new model – negligible difference either way. Same order of cost (one exp(), one division) – negligible difference either way.
Ease of parameter tuning r_op/r_pw jointly govern opinion gating AND self-reliance – tuning one for a target delegation rate can silently distort the other. c alone controls self-reliance; r_op/r_pw only shape the opinion/power kernels – but r_op’s meaning is not comparable across models (III.4), complicating any joint calibration against legacy results.

When legacy may still be preferable. If the research question is specifically about the interaction between responsiveness and self-reliance being the same underlying quantity (e.g. modelling agents whose confidence and pickiness are genuinely the same trait), the legacy formula’s entanglement is a feature, not a bug. It is also the already-published, already-validated basis for Reports 15-19; switching wholesale would break continuity with that body of results unless decision_model = "legacy" is retained for replication (which it is).

6 Part V – Impact on the Simulation

6.1 What we expect to change

  • Cross-group delegation baseline (H1c/H2c, Report 20). Per III.5, the Gaussian kernel plus its shrinking bandwidth should produce lower baseline cross-group attractiveness under polarisation, independent of \(r_{ingroup}\). If Report 20 finds a smaller marginal effect of \(r_{ingroup}\) on cross-group delegation than Report 19 did, that is not necessarily evidence against H1c/H2c – it may simply mean the opinion kernel is already doing part of that work, leaving less room for \(r_{ingroup}\) to add on top. This is a genuine confound to check before interpreting effect sizes across the two reports.
  • Delegation rate range. The "confidence" patch was built specifically to let legacy delegation rates span the full \([0,1]\) range; the Mobius curve does this natively via \(c\). We do not expect a qualitative difference in achievable delegation rates, but the shape of how delegation rate responds to \(r_{op}\) should differ, because \(r_{op}\) now also reshapes the opinion kernel’s bandwidth (III.4), not just its steepness at a fixed point.
  • Voting power concentration (Gini, top-5% share). Indirectly affected through the delegation-rate and chain-length channels above – no direct mechanical change, since compute_power() itself is untouched.
  • Trust dynamics. The trust update rule is identical, but its consequence differs: under legacy, trust cannot destabilise the self-weight formula (III.6); under the new model, strong reward+punish trust interacts with the Mobius ceiling. Expect this to matter mainly in Report 18/20-style trust-heavy diagnostic sweeps (high \(\gamma\), high \(\lambda\)), not in the baseline Report 20 grid where \(\gamma=r_{background} \le 8\) and \(\lambda=0.5\).
  • Stability / convergence. No structural reason to expect a change: both models resolve the delegation decision independently each round from the current opinion/power/trust state; neither introduces new path-dependence.

6.2 Small-scale sensitivity check (this document’s own simulation)

To make the discussion above concrete rather than purely formulaic, this section runs a small, self-contained sweep with the actual simulation code (not a toy re-derivation) – deliberately with no group structure (uniform-random opinions, no minority split), so that only the decision-model effect is visible, uncontaminated by Report 20’s separate ingroup-preference analysis.

sens_seeds <- 1:3
r_vals     <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)

run_sens <- function(seed, r, model) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = 120, n_communities = 1, node_degree = 6,
    T = 12, r_op = r, r_pw = r, p_rewire = 0.05,
    decision_model = model,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5,       # ignored when model == "legacy"
    self_weight_mode = "confidence",  # ignored when model == "gaussian_mobius"
    gamma = r, lambda = 0.5, trust_mode = "reward_punish",
    sigma_opinion = "auto"
  )
  snaps <- res$snapshots |> dplyr::filter(round >= 12 - 4)
  tibble(seed = seed, r = r, model = model,
         delegation_rate  = mean(snaps$delegation_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
         avg_drift        = mean(snaps$avg_drift, na.rm = TRUE),
         gini_power       = mean(snaps$gini_power, na.rm = TRUE),
         top5_power_share = mean(snaps$top5_power_share, na.rm = TRUE))
}

grid_sens <- expand_grid(seed = sens_seeds, r = r_vals, model = c("legacy", "gaussian_mobius"))
sens_raw  <- pmap_dfr(grid_sens, run_sens)

sens_agg <- sens_raw |>
  group_by(r, model) |>
  summarise(across(c(delegation_rate, avg_drift, gini_power, top5_power_share), mean), .groups = "drop")
sens_long <- sens_agg |>
  pivot_longer(c(delegation_rate, avg_drift, gini_power, top5_power_share),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = recode(metric,
                         delegation_rate = "Delegation rate", avg_drift = "Avg. ideological drift",
                         gini_power = "Gini (power)", top5_power_share = "Top-5% power share"))

ggplot(sens_long, aes(r, value, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(legacy = "#d95f02", gaussian_mobius = "#1b9e77")) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = r_vals) +
  labs(title = "Decision-model sensitivity check (no group structure; N=120, T=12, 3 seeds)",
       subtitle = "Same r_op = r_pw = r swept for both models -- see III.4 caveat on comparability",
       x = "r (= r_op = r_pw = gamma)", y = NULL, colour = "decision_model") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

6.3 The new model’s independent self-reliance axis

This is the sensitivity surface that cannot be produced by the legacy model at all without conflating it with \(r_{op}/r_{pw}\) (III.3) – a direct visualisation of what the new parameter buys:

c_vals_heat <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)

run_heat <- function(seed, r, c_self) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = 120, n_communities = 1, node_degree = 6,
    T = 12, r_op = r, r_pw = r, p_rewire = 0.05,
    decision_model = "gaussian_mobius", self_reliance_c = c_self,
    gamma = r, lambda = 0.5, trust_mode = "reward_punish",
    sigma_opinion = "auto"
  )
  snaps <- res$snapshots |> dplyr::filter(round >= 12 - 4)
  tibble(seed = seed, r = r, c_self = c_self,
         delegation_rate = mean(snaps$delegation_rate, na.rm = TRUE))
}

grid_heat <- expand_grid(seed = sens_seeds, r = r_vals, c_self = c_vals_heat)
heat_raw  <- pmap_dfr(grid_heat, run_heat)

heat_agg <- heat_raw |> group_by(r, c_self) |> summarise(delegation_rate = mean(delegation_rate), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(heat_agg, aes(factor(r), factor(c_self), fill = delegation_rate)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", delegation_rate)), size = 3.4,
            colour = ifelse(heat_agg$delegation_rate > 0.5, "white", "black")) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), option = "viridis") +
  labs(title = "gaussian_mobius: delegation rate over (r_op = r_pw, self_reliance_c)",
       subtitle = "r_op/r_pw shape the opinion/power kernels; c independently sets self-reliance -- two orthogonal axes",
       x = "r (= r_op = r_pw = gamma)", y = "self_reliance_c", fill = "delegation\nrate")

Reading across a row (fixed \(r\), varying \(c\)) isolates the self-reliance axis; reading down a column (fixed \(c\), varying \(r\)) isolates the opinion/power responsiveness axis. There is no equivalent clean decomposition available for the legacy model.

7 Part VI – Consolidated Visual Comparison

7.1 Side-by-side decision flow

The structural difference is entirely in the third box: legacy re-derives a fresh quantity from \(j^\*\)’s identity; the new model reuses the number already computed in box 1/2. This single design choice is the source of both the model’s main advantage (decoupled, clean self-reliance parameter, III.3) and its main new risk (out-of-domain \(m\), III.6).

7.2 Combined kernel comparison (opinion + power, both models)

p_op_overlay <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = df_op_old |> filter(r_op %in% c(1, 4)),
            aes(delta, a_op, colour = r_op_label, linetype = "legacy"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = df_op_new |> filter(r_op %in% c(1, 4)),
            aes(delta, a_op, colour = r_op_label, linetype = "gaussian_mobius"), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.7) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(legacy = "dashed", gaussian_mobius = "solid")) +
  labs(title = "Opinion kernel: legacy (dashed) vs. new (solid), r_op in {1, 4}",
       x = expression(Delta), y = expression(a[op]), colour = "r_op", linetype = "model") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_pself_vs_old <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = df_conf, aes(r, w_self, linetype = mode), colour = "#d95f02", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(c = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)), aes(yintercept = c),
             colour = "#1b9e77", linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("text", x = 6, y = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8) + 0.03,
           label = paste0("new model, c=", c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)), colour = "#1b9e77", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Self-vote at identical best neighbour: legacy (orange, varies with r) vs. new (green, flat at c)",
       x = "r (= r_op = r_pw)", y = expression(w[self]~"or"~P[self]), linetype = "legacy mode") +

8.2 Recommendation

For a thesis chapter whose explicit interest is how self-reliance shapes delegation independently of opinion/power responsiveness – which is what Report 20’s design suggests – gaussian_mobius is the better-justified default going forward: it removes an ad hoc patch ("confidence" mode), gives the self-reliance parameter a literal, checkable meaning (\(c = P_{\text{self}}\) at an identical neighbour, for any \(r\)), and its ceiling behaviour is exact rather than asymptotic. legacy remains valuable and should stay available (as it already is, via one argument) for (a) exact replication of Reports 15-19, and (b) any analysis that specifically wants responsiveness and self-confidence to be the same underlying quantity.

8.3 Weaknesses of the new implementation, and concrete fixes

  1. Out-of-domain \(m\) under strong trust (III.6). Fix: clamp before evaluating the curve, preserving the formula’s intent while removing the sign flip:

    p_self_mobius(pmin(w[j_idx], 2), self_reliance_c)

    A one-line change in Network.R’s gaussian_mobius branch. As a diagnostic, it would be worth logging how often the clamp actually binds across Report 20’s grid (likely rare at \(\gamma\le8\), \(\lambda=0.5\), but worth quantifying rather than assuming).

  2. \(r_{op}\) not comparable across models (III.4). Fix: either (a) explicitly caveat any cross-model \(r_{op}\) comparison in the thesis text (the honest, zero-code option), or (b) recalibrate the gaussian_mobius sweep so its half-attractiveness distance matches the legacy sweep’s fixed \(\Delta=0.5\) reference by construction – i.e. choose \(r_{op}\) values from \(r_{op} = \sqrt{2\ln2}/\Delta^\star\) for a chosen target \(\Delta^\star\), rather than reusing Report 19’s raw numbers verbatim.

  3. No sensitivity instrumentation yet for \(c\) specifically. Report 20’s grid does not currently sweep self_reliance_c at all (it is fixed at \(0.5\) throughout, per its setup chunk). Given III.3 identifies this as the headline new capability, a supplementary sweep over \(c\) (holding \(r_{ingroup}\) and \(r_{background}\) fixed) would make direct use of the model’s main advantage rather than leaving it implicit.
